asr.full_text: So hey, we just got to Iceland. We're really excited. We invited about 200 of our friends to fly on out and come check out our data centers. We got a couple of buses here. We're going to pack everyone in, go check out the data center, the Bitcoin mine where we process all these Bitcoin and blockchain transactions around the world. And then we're going to have a big lunch and then we're going to hit up the Blue Lagoon. So it should be a good day. ... ... Hey guys, I'm G-Live from Malaysia. My name is Laurie Warshaw, I live in San Diego, California. My name is Mike, I'm from Calgary, Canada. My name is Joi Zervalakis, I am from Tropical Island, Guam. Hey there, this is Kevin Topino, I am in Reykjavik, Iceland. And what's going on is Bitcoin, baby. To be honest with you, I'm super excited and fired up. I am fortunate enough to be part of the BitClub network, which means I mine Bitcoin. I've been living on Bitcoin since November 26, 2014. You're either the needle or the thread. Get on the bus! So, we just made it to the data center, we just had our tour, to check out all our equipment, we've got lots of team members with us and it's pretty exciting to actually see all the machines at work, 24-7 right here in Iceland. So this is an ant miner, this is the S5. When we started it was the S3s, the S5s, to the S7s, to the S9s. So this tech keeps getting faster and the chips smaller. More efficient, I think this is the 28 nanometer chip. We now have 16 nanometer chips. And by the time you guys are watching this, we might even have like 10 nanometer chips. So it gets smaller, faster, more efficient, less electricity, and these things just crank away. There's thousands and thousands of these things in this data center here. And as you can see, you gotta have a fan because it creates a lot of heat. But this is basically it. This is a machine that prints money literally this is a machine that prints money in the form of Bitcoin it helps us process all the Bitcoin and blockchain transactions of all around the world it all happens here so it turned out to be a pretty successful day. We made it to the data center with about 200 people, we had four buses full, and the weather turned out to be pretty awesome. Great lunch and everyone is so excited. Iceland I would say was a home run now its off to New Hampshire to block fest. Thank you.
